title: A platform package deleted by `git add -A` would land on dev: lore's set-comparison runs only on a release dispatch, never on a PR
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-15, prompted by a REAL incident in quest-cli rather than a hypothetical. WHAT HAPPENED TO QUEST, in their words and their measurement. A tracker-only PR -- one .quest/ file -- went red reproducibly on their source-gates job: git diff --stat 66a7f7d 67be2b7 -- npm/ npm/quest-darwin-arm64/LICENSE | 21 ----- npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest | Bin 64634978 -> 0 bytes npm/quest-darwin-arm64/package.json | 21 ----- Those files were absent from the working tree when `git add -A` ran. Nothing in the session touched them. `git add -A` STAGES A DELETION FOR A TRACKED FILE THAT IS MERELY MISSING, so the commit deleted an entire platform package. Afterwards the index matched the working tree, so `git status` reported CLEAN and `git diff HEAD -- npm/` was EMPTY. Every command anyone would reach for said nothing was wrong. Their commit message and PR body both said "tracker-only" and both were false. Their scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs:19 caught it -- readdir(npm) returned 5 against 6 declared optionalDependencies. WHAT THIS REPOSITORY WOULD HAVE DONE: LANDED IT. ci.yml -> no reference to npm/ anywhere. No PR-time check. package.json scripts -> no check:packages, no equivalent. release.yml:134-141 -> DOES compare the declared platform set against root optionalDependencies keys... but release.yml is `on: workflow_dispatch` ONLY (line 14-15), so it never fires on a push, a PR, or a tag. So lore has the right check and runs it at the wrong time. A platform package silently deleted by `git add -A` on a tracker-only commit would pass every gate on the PR, land on dev, and first be detected during a RELEASE DISPATCH. That is the precise failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about: "a gate that is wrong fails only during a release." Worse, the detection would arrive at the moment it is most expensive and most likely to be misread. A release operator seeing "platform set mismatch" mid-dispatch has to decide whether the release machinery is broken or the repository is, under time pressure, with the tag possibly already cut. MY OWN TREE IS INTACT, checked rather than assumed: npm/ holds 6 directories, each containing exactly package.json. git ls-tree -r v0.7.0 -- npm/ shows the same 6 files -- package.json only. git diff --stat 41ac5a65 HEAD -- npm/ is empty: nothing today touched it. Note the design difference that makes lore's surface SMALLER but not safer: lore does not commit platform binaries (they are built in CI), so each npm// holds one file where quest's holds three including a 64MB binary. Fewer files to lose, and the same `git add -A` mechanism loses them just as silently. A smaller blast radius is not a guard. THIS IS ALSO THE DECLARED-SUBJECT CLAUSE OF THE SHIPPED-README CONTRACT, ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION. That clause was argued on a file APPEARING in a package directory and changing A1's subject silently. Quest's incident is a file DISAPPEARING from a tree that reports clean. A discovered set changes membership in both directions and neither is announced; an enumerated one does not. Their closed `files` list is what made the drift detectable, and it detected a case neither of us imagined when arguing for it. REMEDY, and the cheap version is genuinely cheap: 1. A `check:packages` script asserting readdir(npm/) equals the root optionalDependencies key set, plus each npm/

/package.json being present and parseable. Wire it into ci.yml so it runs on every PR. 2. Give each npm//package.json an explicit `files` list. They currently have NONE, so npm packs whatever the directory contains -- today exactly package.json, but the set is discovered rather than declared. This is the same clause as the README contract's A1 and should land with it. 3. Consider moving release.yml's existing set-comparison into the shared script so there is ONE assertion invoked from two places, rather than two that can disagree. CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE: this gap was not found by inspection here. quest-cli hit the real thing, reported it against its own interest, and I checked whether lore would have caught it. It would not have.
plan:
Add scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs asserting readdir(npm/) equals the root optionalDependencies key set as @opum-ai/lore-, each npm/

/package.json present, parseable, name matching, with an explicit files list; one message per problem, exit 1 on any, exit 0 clean, non-zero when it cannot evaluate.
Give each npm/<platform>/package.json an explicit files list, decided from what release.yml actually places in the dir.
Wire package.json check:packages and one ci.yml job on every PR; not a required context, no ruleset change.
release.yml calls the same script for its set comparison so there is ONE assertion invoked from two places.
test/check-package-artifacts.test.ts drives the script against fixture dirs, clean green, each failure red for its own reason, plus wiring tests; mutation-check each.
CI proof: one commit deleting a platform dir goes red on the new job with the set-mismatch message, revert goes green, other jobs green on both heads; record run ids, heads, message, Bun version.
implementationNotes:
SESSION HANDOFF 2026-09-15. FILED, UNSTARTED. Nothing has been implemented; the description holds the full measurement.

WHY IT IS HIGH AND SHOULD NOT BE DEFERRED BEHIND THE README WORK: the failure is
SILENT and lands on dev. `git add -A` stages a deletion for any tracked file merely
MISSING from the tree, and afterwards the index matches the tree -- so `git status`
reports clean and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Every command anyone would reach for
confirms nothing is wrong. quest-cli lost an entire platform package this way on a
tracker-only PR whose message said "tracker-only" and was false.

THE EXPOSURE IS STRUCTURAL HERE, not incidental: `git add -A .quest` is MANDATORY
in this repository because `quest complete` renames tasks/ -> completed/ and a bare
`git add` leaves a dangling delete. So the flag this repo requires is the flag that
launders an unrelated deletion into a tracker commit. quest-cli has offered to file
a quest-side change where `quest complete` stages its own rename, which would let a
scoped `git add .quest` suffice; that offer is open and unanswered.

INTERIM DISCIPLINE, already in use in this session's later commits and worth
keeping until the check exists: scope the stage (`git add -A .quest`, never bare
`git add -A`) and read `git diff --cached --name-status` before committing. A
"tracker-only" claim is checkable in one command.

STATE VERIFIED AT HANDOFF, so the successor need not re-derive it:
  npm/ holds 6 dirs, each containing exactly package.json
  git ls-tree -r v0.7.0 -- npm/  shows the same 6 files
  git diff --stat 41ac5a65 HEAD -- npm/  is empty
  npm/*/package.json have NO `files` field -- npm packs whatever the dir holds
  .gitignore includes `npm/*/bin/`, so built binaries would be ignored if present
The tree is intact. This is a missing GATE, not an active corruption.

DESIGN NOTE THAT IS EASY TO MISREAD AS SAFETY: lore builds platform binaries in CI
rather than committing them, so each dir holds one file where quest's holds three.
That is a smaller blast radius, NOT a guard.

REMEDY, in the description, unchanged: a check:packages script asserting
readdir(npm/) equals the root optionalDependencies key set, wired into ci.yml so it
runs on every PR; explicit `files` lists on each platform package.json; and ideally
ONE shared assertion invoked from both ci.yml and release.yml rather than two that
can disagree. release.yml:134-141 already has the comparison -- it is
`on: workflow_dispatch` only, which is the entire defect.

PROOF, per the fleet rule and this session's own experience with clause 3: prove
rejection AND acceptance as two separate measurements -- delete a platform dir and
see the new job go red for ITS OWN reason (read the message, not just the colour),
then restore and see the tree green. Confirm the other jobs are green on both SHAs.

FILES DECISION (plan step 2), measured rather than assumed. The platform tarball is NOT packed from npm/<platform>/ as it sits in git. benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts stagePlatformPackage() (lines 654-657) builds a scratch root holding an empty bin/ plus a copy of npm/<platform>/package.json; the compiled binary is written to <stage>/bin/<matrix.binary> (line 305) and 'npm pack .' runs inside that stage (line 314). release.yml's package job then copies those already-packed tarballs out of the qualification artifacts (release.yml, 'Assemble the exact matching-host-qualified platform tarballs') and packs only the root launcher. No LICENSE or README is staged into a platform root -- stageRootPackage() copies those for the launcher only. So exactly two files ship per platform package: package.json (npm always includes it regardless of files) and bin/lore, or bin/lore.exe on win32-*. The files list is therefore ["bin/lore"] for darwin-*/linux-* and ["bin/lore.exe"] for win32-*: the exact filename rather than the bin/ directory, because the point of the closed-set argument is that membership is declared, and a directory glob is a discovered set one level down. .gitignore's npm/*/bin/ line is why each directory holds only package.json in git today. The shared script asserts only that files is an explicit non-empty string list; asserting files against the matrix binary name would be a natural addition to release.yml's per-platform field loop, deliberately not made here to keep that job's behaviour otherwise identical.

MUTATION MATRIX (plan step 5), each row: mutate one file, run the targeted test, restore from a pristine copy, cmp-verified identical afterwards. All 19 CAUGHT. M01 script: drop the missing-direction push -> 'npm/ directory is missing' fails. M02 drop the extra-direction push -> 'does not declare' fails. M03 swallow the parse error -> 'does not parse' fails. M04 drop the name check -> 'name disagrees' fails. M05 drop the files-is-array check -> 'no explicit files list' fails. M06 drop the files-non-empty check -> 'files list is empty' fails. M07 drop the --platforms comparison -> 'release matrix that disagrees' fails. M08 main() returns 0 on cannot-evaluate -> 'not a directory is exit 2' fails. M09 drop the manifest-exists check -> 'no package.json in it' fails. M10 print only the first problem -> 'every problem' fails. M11 treat missing npm/ as all-present -> 'npm/ missing entirely' fails. M12 ci.yml: replace 'bun run check:packages' with echo -> wiring test fails. M13 ci.yml: add needs: check to the job -> fails. M14 ci.yml: append '|| true' -> fails. M15 release.yml: replace the script call with echo -> fails. M16 release.yml: append '|| true' -> fails. M17 release.yml: reintroduce 'const declaredPkgNames' inline -> 'no longer carries its own inline copy' fails. M18 package.json: check:packages -> 'true' -> fails. M19 real tree: mv npm/win32-arm64 away -> both 'real repository' acceptance tests fail with '::error::platform set mismatch: root package.json optionalDependencies declares @opum-ai/lore-win32-arm64, but npm/win32-arm64/ is missing (npm/ holds [darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-x64])'; restored -> both pass. Local toolchain: bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0. bun test test/check-package-artifacts.test.ts 22/22, sibling workflow tests 88 pass, bun run lint 0, bun run typecheck 0, bun run lint:shell 0, bun run check:packages 0 on the real tree. SCOPE NOTE: test/ci-workflow.test.ts holds an exact list of ci.yml job ids and would go red on the two required lint/typecheck/test contexts with any new job, so one line ('package-set') was added there; that file was outside the stated exclusive scope and is called out in the PR.

CI PROOF, REJECTION HALF (plan step 6). PR #122. Violation commit b6e8018ddafeacdf3827afee79cb4148cbb6f151 (`git rm -r npm/win32-arm64`, staged diff read back as exactly `D npm/win32-arm64/package.json`). Run 35029093828, resolved by --commit <sha>, status completed, conclusion failure. Job 'platform package set (npm/ vs optionalDependencies)' (job id 104583480010) RED for its own reason; log lines verbatim: 'bun 1.3.14' / 'node v22.23.2' / '##[error]platform set mismatch: root package.json optionalDependencies declares @opum-ai/lore-win32-arm64, but npm/win32-arm64/ is missing (npm/ holds [darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-x64])' / '1 platform package problem(s) under /home/runner/work/lore-cli/lore-cli. If a directory under npm/ is missing and nothing in your change touched it, look at how it was staged: `git add -A` stages a deletion for any tracked file merely absent from the tree.' / 'error: script "check:packages" exited with code 1'. Green on the same head: ladybug benchmark smoke, mkdocs scaffold smoke, Tracker integrity, config test (newest Bun), lore check (docs gate), explorer browser qualification, compile smoke (ubuntu), docker e2e harness, docusaurus scaffold smoke; promotion guards skipped as designed. TWO OTHER JOBS ALSO RED, and this is a finding rather than noise: 'lint · typecheck · test' on ubuntu-latest (4 fail / 3141 pass) and windows-latest (4 fail / 3003 pass), identical four tests on both. Two are this PR's own acceptance tests ('the real repository, which is what ci.yml gates' and '... against release.yml's matrix names'), which assert the real tree passes the script -- precedent: shipped-readme-version.test.ts runs --check against the real README the same way. The OTHER TWO ARE PRE-EXISTING: test/repository-location.test.ts 'canonical repository location > every release manifest uses the exact canonical GitHub repository URL' (line 147) and 'canonical npm package family > the launcher and all platform manifests use the exact @opum-ai names' (line 201) both readFileSync npm/<platform>/package.json for a hardcoded platform list, so a deleted directory throws ENOENT inside them. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: the description's claim that this repository WOULD HAVE LANDED a git add -A deletion is falsified for the pure-deletion case -- both required test contexts already went red on it, incidentally, via ENOENT in an identity test. What that incidental catch does NOT give and this change does: a named single-purpose verdict with a diagnosis ('platform set mismatch ... npm/win32-arm64/ is missing' rather than 'ENOENT' inside a repository-URL test), the extra-directory direction, the explicit files list, a comparison DERIVED from package.json rather than from a platform list hardcoded inside a test about repository URLs, and the release-side shared call site that ties the setup matrix into the same comparison. Revert commit e569f537f7fba40c6163b87d71b3de5c762988f8 pushed after run 35029093828 completed (ci.yml cancels in-progress PR runs on a new push, so pushing earlier would have destroyed this measurement); its run is the acceptance half, recorded separately.

CI PROOF, ACCEPTANCE HALF (plan step 6). Revert commit e569f537f7fba40c6163b87d71b3de5c762988f8 (reverts b6e8018d; diff is exactly `A npm/win32-arm64/package.json`). Run 35029689728, resolved by --commit <sha>, status completed, conclusion success. EVERY job green: platform package set (npm/ vs optionalDependencies) (job 104585020103), lint · typecheck · test (ubuntu-latest), lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest), Tracker integrity, lore check (docs gate), docker e2e harness, compile smoke (ubuntu), config test (newest Bun), ladybug benchmark smoke, explorer browser qualification, mkdocs scaffold smoke, docusaurus scaffold smoke; promotion guards skipped as designed. package-set log verbatim: 'bun 1.3.14' / 'node v22.23.2' / 'npm/ holds exactly the 6 platform packages root package.json declares ([darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-arm64, win32-x64]), each with an explicit files list'. Same Bun (1.3.14) and Node (v22.23.2) on both halves, so the two runs measured the same toolchain; local workstation was bun 1.3.14 / node v24.20.0. SUMMARY OF THE TWO-MEASUREMENT PROOF: red run 35029093828 on b6e8018d with the set-mismatch message and no unrelated failure; green run 35029689728 on e569f537 with every job green. Both resolved by head SHA, never by --limit 1. PR #122 left unmerged; per CLAUDE.md it touches release.yml and scripts/ and wants a reviewer pass. Recorded on the PR as two comments.

REVIEWER SHOULD-FIXES FOLDED INTO PR #122 (verdict: safe to land, release safety verified byte-for-byte). (1) files CONTENT, not presence: the script now asserts files equals exactly ["bin/lore.exe"] when the os token before the first '-' is win32, else ["bin/lore"] -- the same convention release.yml derives `binary` from -- with a message naming actual vs expected and the manifest path. Reviewer's measurement that motivated it: a darwin-arm64 fixture declaring ["bin/lore.exe"] exited 0 and `npm pack --dry-run` on that manifest yielded ONE file, package.json only. (2) LORE_PACKAGE_CHECK_ROOT env fallback deleted; --root is the only way to repoint the gate; success line now prints `under <root>` like the failure line, and a test runs the script WITHOUT --root under that env name set to /nonexistent and asserts exit 0 with the real root named. (3) Four untested branches now have reject rows: a non-directory entry under npm/, an optionalDependencies key not of the form @opum-ai/lore-<platform> (fsevents), a non-string files entry (["bin/lore", 3]), and --platforms with no value -> exit 2. (4) Nit taken: hidden DIRECTORIES under npm/ now count toward the set (npm/.stale-darwin-x64/ -> extra-directory finding); only hidden FILES are skipped, so .DS_Store stays green; test covers both halves. NEW MUTATION ROWS, same method (mutate, targeted test, restore, cmp-verified): M20 files content check disabled -> 'names the wrong binary' fails. M21 same mutation -> 'extra entry nothing qualified' fails. M22 os-token ternary inverted -> 'non-Windows binary' fails (FIRST DRAFT NOT CAUGHT: the assertion lacked the manifest path and the inverted script emitted the identical sentence for the five non-win32 manifests; fixed by asserting the path, and the same precision added to the empty-list and extra-entry rows). M23 non-string predicate disabled -> 'non-string entry' fails. M24 isDirectory branch disabled -> 'non-directory entry under npm' fails. M25 old hidden-skip order restored -> 'hidden DIRECTORY' fails. M26 scope-prefix check disabled -> 'not an @opum-ai' fails. M27 --platforms value guard disabled -> 'platforms with no value' fails. M28 env fallback reintroduced -> 'no environment variable' fails (FIRST DRAFT NOT CAUGHT: the test passed --root, which overrides the default so the fallback never engaged; fixed by running without --root and asserting the `under <root>` line). Original matrix re-run against the revised script: M01-M05, M07-M18 all still CAUGHT; M06 (the separate empty-list branch) no longer exists -- its case was re-measured under the M20 mutation and 'files list is empty' fails there, so it is covered by the content check. Totals: 17 re-run + 1 re-measured + 9 new = 27 rows, 27 caught. Local: bun test test/check-package-artifacts.test.ts 31/31; bun run lint 0 (3 pre-existing warnings elsewhere); bun run typecheck 0; bun run check:packages 0 on the real tree, success line 'npm/ holds exactly the 6 platform packages root package.json declares ([...]) under <root>, each listing exactly its own binary in files'. NO NEW CI VIOLATION PROOF: the wiring (ci.yml job, release.yml step, package.json script) is unchanged by these fixes, so the two existing proof runs stand -- 35029093828 red on b6e8018d with the set-mismatch message, 35029689728 green on e569f537 -- and the fixes are proven by the mutation rows above; the PR's own CI run on the new head is the acceptance measurement for them.
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #122 (fix/LCLI-513-package-set-gate-on-every-pr, base dev). ONE assertion, scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs, invoked from two call sites: ci.yml job 'platform package set (npm/ vs optionalDependencies)' via `bun run check:packages` on every pull request and on push to main (not a required context; no ruleset touched), and release.yml verify-versions via `node scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs --platforms "$PLATFORM_NAMES_SPACE"`, whose inline set comparison was removed. It asserts: the directories under npm/ equal root optionalDependencies as @opum-ai/lore-<dir> in both directions; each npm/<dir>/package.json exists, parses, carries the name its directory implies, and declares files EXACTLY as ["bin/lore.exe"] when the os token before the first "-" is win32, else ["bin/lore"] (reviewer should-fix: a darwin manifest declaring bin/lore.exe passed a presence-only check and npm-packed to package.json alone); foreign optionalDependencies keys, stray files under npm/, hidden directories (counted; hidden files skipped so .DS_Store stays green) and a matrix that disagrees with package.json are each named. Exit 0 clean, 1 on any finding (one ::error:: per problem), 2 on usage or a tree it cannot evaluate; a missing npm/ is exit 1 naming every declared package. --root is the only way to repoint it; the env fallback was deleted and a test pins that.

FILES DECISION, with evidence: benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts stagePlatformPackage() (lines 654-657) stages a scratch root holding a copy of npm/<name>/package.json plus bin/, the binary is compiled to <stage>/bin/<matrix.binary> (line 305), and `npm pack .` runs in that stage (line 314); release.yml's package job copies those tarballs out of the qualification artifacts and packs only the launcher. No LICENSE or README is staged for platform packages. So exactly package.json (always packed) and the one binary ship, and each npm/<platform>/package.json now declares that binary by filename.

CI PROOF, two measurements resolved by head SHA: run 35029093828 on b6e8018d (git rm -r npm/win32-arm64) RED with '##[error]platform set mismatch: root package.json optionalDependencies declares @opum-ai/lore-win32-arm64, but npm/win32-arm64/ is missing (npm/ holds [darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-x64])', bun 1.3.14 / node v22.23.2; run 35029689728 on e569f537 (the revert) GREEN on every job, same toolchain. Local: 31 tests in test/check-package-artifacts.test.ts, 27 mutation rows all caught (17 original rows re-run after the reviewer's fixes, the retired empty-list row re-measured under the content check, plus 9 new), lint/typecheck/lint:shell/check:packages all exit 0.

CORRECTION TO THIS TASK'S OWN PREMISE, measured on the violation run: test/repository-location.test.ts:147 and :201 already readFileSync every npm/<platform>/package.json from a hardcoded list, so a pure deletion already turned BOTH required 'lint · typecheck · test' contexts red -- incidentally, as an ENOENT inside an identity test. 'This repository would have LANDED it' is therefore false for that case. What this change adds is a named single-purpose diagnosis instead of an ENOENT in a repository-URL test, the extra-directory direction, the explicit files list and its content check, a comparison derived from package.json rather than a hardcoded platform list, and one shared assertion at both call sites so the release-time and PR-time verdicts cannot drift. Reviewer verdict on #122: safe to land, release safety verified byte-for-byte; its three should-fixes (files content, env fallback removal, four untested branches) and the hidden-directory nit are folded into the PR. Scope deviation: one line in test/ci-workflow.test.ts (its exact ci.yml job list). Not merged by this session.
